newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 21.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 21.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:

** The Reserve Bank of India has directed the stock market regulator (SEBI) to cap foreign institutional investors' (FIIs) exposure in debt floatations by Indian corporates, the Financial Express reports.
SEBI had recently allowed FIIs to invest 100 percent of their funds in debt issues.

** India's industry ministry has approved a $600-million plan by Tata Industries and Singapore International Airlines (SIA) to set up a domestic Indian airline, the Press Trust of India (PTI) reported on Monday.

The industry ministry sent the plan, cleared early this month by the Foreign Investment Promotion Board (FIPB), with favourable recommendations to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's cabinet last week, PTI said.

** The government approved a proposal on Monday for allowing automatic approvals by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) up to 74 percent foreign equity in nine categories of industries, the Business Standard reports.

These industries included electricity generation and transmission, construction, mining, services and basic metals and alloys industries. The paper said the list of automatic approvals by the RBI had been expanded by including three industries relating to mining activity for foreign equity up to 50 percent and 13 additional industries for foreign equity up to 51 percent.
** Dena Bank, the first in a series of Indian state-run banks to launch new issues, was listed on Monday and traded below its issue price.
Shares of Dena Bank closed at 27 rupees on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). Dena raised 1.8 billion rupees in November through an initial public offer at 30 rupees a share.

** Barclays De Zoette Wedd, the investment banking arm of the British bank, Barclays Bank has given up plans for a joint venture in stock broking and has now decided to go it alone, the Economic Times reports.
** The Indian rupee opened steady against the dollar at 35.85/86 on Tuesday. The rupee is expected to move in a tight range and end the day at 35.84/85, a pattern seen for the past several days.
The BSE's top 30-share index .BSESN closed 32.86 points, or 0.96 percent lower, at 3,389.49, off 3,478.0, the intra-day high.
** The 50-stock National Stock Exchange .NSEI fell 24.75 points, or 2.6 percent, to 977.0.
** The Delhi index .DE lost 15.95 points, to 718.56.
** The Madras index .MDSI eased 49.58 points, to 3,267.40.
